text: Every household, commercial establishment, and institution within BBMP limits shall segregate solid waste at source into three categories: wet (biodegradable) waste, dry (recyclable) waste, and domestic hazardous waste. Mixed waste shall not be handed over to collection staff.

A first-time violation of Section 3.1 shall attract a spot fine of INR 100 for individual households and INR 500 for bulk waste generators (establishments generating more than 100 kg of waste per day). Repeat violations within a 90-day period shall attract a fine of INR 500 for households and INR 2,000 for bulk generators, and collection may be suspended for up to 7 days.

Where ward-level monitoring data shows that more than 25% of collected waste from a ward is improperly segregated over any rolling 30-day period, the ward's Health Inspector shall initiate a mandatory door-to-door awareness drive within 15 days, in coordination with the local Resident Welfare Association (RWA).

Bulk waste generators must process biodegradable waste on-site through composting or biomethanation, or hand it over to BBMP-authorized processing agencies. Non-compliance shall attract a daily penalty of INR 5,000 until compliance is demonstrated.
Wet waste shall be collected daily (including Sundays) from all notified collection points. Dry waste shall be collected twice a week on a fixed schedule published by the respective ward office.

Littering or dumping of any waste in public spaces, storm water drains, lakes, or vacant sites is prohibited. Violation shall attract a fine of INR 200 for individuals and INR 2,000 for commercial entities per instance, in addition to mandatory clean-up cost recovery.

jurisdiction: Karnataka State Pollution Control Board (KSPCB), applicable within BBMP limits
text: These rules apply to electrical and electronic equipment (EEE) and their components, consumables, parts, and spares that become e-waste, including batteries covered under the Battery Waste Management Rules.

jurisdiction: Karnataka State Pollution Control Board (KSPCB), applicable within BBMP limits
text: BBMP shall designate at least one authorized e-waste collection point per ward. Residents must deposit e-waste only at authorized collection points or through authorized dismantlers/recyclers, and shall not dispose of e-waste with mixed municipal solid waste.

jurisdiction: Karnataka State Pollution Control Board (KSPCB), applicable within BBMP limits
section: Section 3.5: Penalty for Improper E-Waste Disposal
text: Disposal of e-waste along with regular municipal solid waste, or dumping in public spaces, is prohibited under Section 3.4 and shall attract a fine of INR 1,000 per instance for individuals, and INR 10,000 for bulk consumers such as offices and institutions.

jurisdiction: Karnataka State Pollution Control Board (KSPCB), applicable within BBMP limits
section: Section 4.2: Collection Frequency at Ward Collection Points
text: Authorized e-waste collection points shall be operational at least twice a month, with collected e-waste transported to registered dismantlers within 15 days of receipt.

jurisdiction: Karnataka State Pollution Control Board (KSPCB), applicable within BBMP limits
text: Producers of electrical and electronic equipment are responsible for establishing collection mechanisms and meeting extended producer responsibility (EPR) targets as notified annually by the Central Pollution Control Board.

jurisdiction: Karnataka State Government, enforced by BBMP within city limits
text: The manufacture, sale, storage, and use of the following single-use plastic items is prohibited: plastic carry bags below 120 microns, plastic cutlery, plastic straws, plastic flags, plastic banners below 100 microns, and thermocol (polystyrene) decorative items.

jurisdiction: Karnataka State Government, enforced by BBMP within city limits
section: Section 2.3: Penalty for Sale or Use of Banned Items
text: First-time violation by a vendor or commercial establishment shall attract a fine of INR 5,000. Second violation shall attract a fine of INR 10,000. Third and subsequent violations shall attract a fine of INR 25,000 along with potential cancellation of trade license.

jurisdiction: Karnataka State Government, enforced by BBMP within city limits
text: An individual found using banned single-use plastic items in public shall be fined INR 200 per instance.

jurisdiction: Karnataka State Government, enforced by BBMP within city limits
text: BBMP Marshals and designated Health Inspectors are authorized to conduct surprise inspections at commercial establishments, wholesale markets, and public events to check compliance.

doc_title: Wet Waste Segregation Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
jurisdiction: BBMP, issued by Solid Waste Management Cell
text: Households generating less than 5 kg of wet waste per day are encouraged to adopt home composting using pit, pot, or vermicompost methods. BBMP provides subsidized composting kits through ward offices.

doc_title: Wet Waste Segregation Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
jurisdiction: BBMP, issued by Solid Waste Management Cell
text: Apartment complexes and gated communities with more than 50 units must install and operate an on-site organic waste converter (OWC) or community composting unit with a minimum processing capacity matching 80% of the complex's estimated daily wet waste generation.

doc_title: Wet Waste Segregation Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
jurisdiction: BBMP, issued by Solid Waste Management Cell
text: Ward Health Inspectors shall conduct random waste audits at collection points at least twice a month, recording the proportion of segregated versus mixed waste received. Data shall be uploaded to the BBMP Solid Waste Dashboard within 48 hours of the audit.

doc_title: Wet Waste Segregation Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
jurisdiction: BBMP, issued by Solid Waste Management Cell
text: If a ward's audit data shows a segregation compliance rate below 75% for two consecutive audit cycles, the ward shall be flagged for escalated enforcement under Bylaw Section 4.2, including intensified awareness drives and increased spot-fine enforcement.
